Bank Tellers process cash receipts and payments, deposits and withdrawals, transfers and remittances, account openings and closures, negotiable instrument settlement, and account services at bank branches. They verify customer identity and documents, operate core banking systems, and complete reconciliation, serving as the bank's first service point for retail and corporate customers.

entries: Bank tellers process cash receipts and payments, deposits and withdrawals, transfers and remittances, account openings and closures, negotiable instrument settlement, and account services at bank branches. They verify customer identity and documents, operate core banking systems, and complete reconciliation.
Process cash receipts and payments, count and sort cash, transfer end-of-day cash boxes, and ensure records match physical cash.
Handle account opening, closure, loss reporting, transfers, remittances, and related account transactions.
Verify customer identity documents, transaction documents, and signatures, and perform anti-money laundering and compliance checks.
Review and settle checks, cashier's checks, drafts, and related negotiable instruments.
Answer customer questions, introduce basic products such as deposits and wealth management, and refer customers.
Balance at the end of the day, print transaction records, organize documents, and archive and report them according to policy.

paragraphs: Before opening, reconcile the vault and collect the cash box. Process a continuous queue throughout the morning, from cash deposits and withdrawals to bill payments and information changes. Reconcile at midday, and immediately review video to explain any cash overage or shortage. Handle complex transactions and complaints in the afternoon. Near closing, complete end-of-day balancing, count and seal cash, and return it to the vault. Leave only after the system balances.

In short: complete customers' cash and account transactions at the counter. Duties include counting and processing cash, opening accounts and making transfers, settling negotiable instruments, verifying identity and compliance, answering questions, and balancing at day-end. Employment is projected to decline to 302,500 by 2034, a net decrease of about 44,900 jobs, with approximately 29,800 openings annually. Median annual pay in 2026 is about $39,300 (BLS OOH, 2026).

AI will not replace bank tellers, but it will sharply reduce pure counter operations. Mobile banking, smart teller machines, and RPA reconciliation take over standardized transactions, shifting tellers from keyboard entry toward exception handling, explaining rules, and managing customer relationships. Tellers who only process transactions mechanically face displacement, while those who handle complex transactions and enforce compliance become more valuable.
